<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Clarifying widget data flow and update logic**

The app updates device locations and map snapshots by writing shared data and triggering widget timeline reloads, which happen on location cache or device list changes. Widget timelines fetch fresh data every 15 minutes or reload sooner when the app signals changes; however, map snapshots update only via the app, so if it’s not running, the displayed map may lag behind recent server locations despite timeline data refreshing.</details></think>

Widget update flow and display logic

- Timeline cadence: Both widgets build a single-entry timeline and ask WidgetKit to refresh every 15 minutes (`policy: .after(next)`), so they only fetch on that cadence unless timelines are reloaded explicitly.
```33:41:miataruWidgets/DeviceLocationTextWidget.swift
    func timeline(for configuration: DeviceSelectionIntent, in context: Context) async -> Timeline<DeviceLocationEntry> {
        let entry = await buildEntry(configuration: configuration)
        let next = Calendar.current.date(byAdding: .minute, value: 15, to: Date()) ?? Date().addingTimeInterval(900)
        return Timeline(entries: [entry], policy: .after(next))
    }
```

- Data source for each timeline: When a timeline is requested, the loader reads the last app-written payload from the App Group, figures out the selected device ID (intent → cached list → first configured), and, if it has server config, calls Miataru to fetch fresh locations for the target + own device. It merges those into the payload, persists back to the shared file, and returns the selected device and own-device record for distance calculations.
```15:58:miataruWidgets/WidgetTimelineDataLoader.swift
    static func loadEntryData(configuration: DeviceSelectionIntent) async -> (WidgetSharedPayload, WidgetDeviceData?) {
        let cachedPayload = SharedWidgetDataManager.read()
        let config = SharedWidgetConfigManager.read()
        let targetID = configuration.device?.id
            ?? cachedPayload?.devices.first?.id
            ?? config?.deviceIDs.first
        ...
        let locations = try await MiataruAPIClient.getLocation(
            serverURL: serverURL,
            forDeviceIDs: requestIDs,
            requestingDeviceID: config.ownDeviceID
        )
        payload = merge(locations, into: payload, cached: cachedPayload, ownDeviceID: config.ownDeviceID ?? payload.ownDeviceID)
        SharedWidgetDataManager.write(payload)
        let selectedDeviceID = targetID ?? requestIDs.first ?? cachedDeviceIDs.first
        let device = selectedDeviceID.flatMap { id in payload.devices.first(where: { $0.id == id }) }
        return (payload, device)
    }
```

- How the main app keeps the shared payload fresh: Whenever a device list or cached location changes, the app rebuilds the payload from `KnownDeviceStore` + `DeviceLocationCacheStore`, writes it to the App Group, updates widget config (server URL, device IDs, own ID), and forces WidgetKit to reload all timelines—this is what enables faster-than-15-minute updates while the app is active or recently active.
```21:78:miataru/SettingsManagers/WidgetDataSyncCoordinator.swift
    static func syncAllDevices() {
        let devices = KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices
        let locations = DeviceLocationCacheStore.shared.locations
        let ownDeviceID = thisDeviceIDManager.shared.deviceID

        let payload = buildPayload(devices: devices, locations: locations, ownDeviceID: ownDeviceID)
        SharedWidgetDataManager.write(payload)
        syncWidgetConfig(
            serverURL: SettingsManager.shared.miataruServerURL,
            deviceIDs: devices.map { $0.DeviceID },
            ownDeviceID: ownDeviceID,
            shouldReloadTimelines: false
        )
        WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines()
    }
```

- What triggers app-side syncs: Each time a location is cached (own or remote), the cache writes, optionally kicks off reverse geocoding, then calls `syncAllDevices()` and generates map snapshots for that device. Device list changes also call `syncAllDevices()`.
```133:178:miataru/SettingsManagers/App Settings/Devices/DeviceLocationCacheStore.swift
    func setLocation(for deviceID: String, latitude: Double, longitude: Double, accuracy: Double, timestamp: Date, batteryLevel: Double? = nil, altitude: Double? = nil, speed: Double? = nil) {
        ...
        if let idx = locations.firstIndex(where: { $0.deviceID == deviceID }) {
            ...
            WidgetDataSyncCoordinator.syncAllDevices()
        } else {
            ...
            WidgetDataSyncCoordinator.syncAllDevices()
        }

        if let location = snapshotLocation,
           let device = KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.first(where: { $0.DeviceID == deviceID }) {
            WidgetMapSnapshotGenerator.generateSnapshot(for: device, location: location)
        }
    }
```

- Map snapshots: The app renders light/dark map images with a marker and stores them in the App Group; widgets simply read these PNGs by device ID (preferring light/dark based on color scheme). The widget extension itself does not regenerate snapshots; it depends on the main app having produced them after a location update.
```20:52:miataru/views/Common/WidgetMapSnapshotGenerator.swift
enum WidgetMapSnapshotGenerator {
    static func generateSnapshot(for device: KnownDevice, location: CachedDeviceLocation, size: CGSize = CGSize(width: 400, height: 400)) {
        Task.detached(priority: .utility) {
            ...
            await renderSnapshot(for: device, location: location, coordinate: coordinate, size: size, style: .light)
            await renderSnapshot(for: device, location: location, coordinate: coordinate, size: size, style: .dark)
        }
    }
}
```
```88:126:miataruWidgets/DeviceLocationMapWidget.swift
    private func snapshotLayer(for device: WidgetDeviceData) -> some View {
        let preferredURL: URL? = {
            switch colorScheme {
            case .dark:
                return SharedWidgetDataManager.mapSnapshotURL(for: device.id, style: .dark)
            default:
                return SharedWidgetDataManager.mapSnapshotURL(for: device.id, style: .light)
            }
        }()
        let fallbackURL = SharedWidgetDataManager.mapSnapshotURL(for: device.id)

        if let url = preferredURL ?? fallbackURL,
           let data = try? Data(contentsOf: url),
           let uiImage = UIImage(data: data) {
            return AnyView(
                Image(uiImage: uiImage)
                    .resizable()
                    .scaledToFill()
            )
        }
        ...
    }
```

- Display contents: Both widgets read `WidgetDeviceData` (name, coordinates, locality/country, timestamp, optional accuracy/color) and `ownDevice` to compute distance and “last update” text. The map widget overlays those texts on the snapshot; the text widget shows name, locality, distance, and relative timestamp.

How frequently locations/maps update in practice
- While the app is running or receiving location/cache updates, every change writes to the shared payload, regenerates snapshots, and reloads timelines immediately—widgets should refresh soon after.
- In background/idle, WidgetKit will refresh at the 15-minute cadence using the latest shared payload and will also call the Miataru API itself for the selected/own devices, updating the payload for the next refresh.
- Map images are only refreshed when the main app generates snapshots; if only the widget runs (extension fetch) without the app producing new snapshots, text data can update from API but the map image may stay stale until the app next writes a snapshot.
